blocks.text: This is a Pussy called Miss Moppet, she thinks she has heard a mouse!
This is the Mouse peeping out behind the cupboard, and making fun of Miss Moppet. He is not afraid of a kitten.

blocks.alt: Miss MoppetThis is Miss Moppet jumping just too late.

blocks.text: This is Miss Moppet jumping just too late; she misses the Mouse and hits her own head.
She thinks it is a very hard cupboard!

blocks.alt: She thinks it is a very hard cupboard!
The Mouse watches Miss Moppet from the top of the cupboard.

blocks.text: The Mouse watches Miss Moppet from the top of the cupboard.
Miss Moppet ties up her head in a duster, and sits before the fire.

blocks.alt: Miss Moppet ties up her head in a duster, and sits before the fire.

blocks.text: The Mouse thinks she is looking very ill. He comes sliding down the bell-pull.

blocks.alt: Mouse comes sliding down the bell-pull.
The Mouse comes a little nearer.

blocks.text: Miss Moppet looks worse and worse. The Mouse comes a little nearer.

blocks.alt: Miss Moppet holds her poor head in her paws, and looks at him through a hole in the duster.

blocks.text: Miss Moppet holds her poor head in her paws, and looks at him through a hole in the duster. The Mouse comes very close.
And then all of a sudden—Miss Moppet jumps upon the Mouse!

blocks.alt: Miss Moppet thinks she will tease the Mouse.
She ties him up in the duster...

blocks.text: And because the Mouse has teased Miss Moppet—Miss Moppet thinks she will tease the Mouse; which is not at all nice of Miss Moppet.
She ties him up in the duster, and tosses it about like a ball.

blocks.alt: ...and tosses it about like a ball.

blocks.text: But she forgot about that hole in the duster; and when she untied it—there was no Mouse!

blocks.alt: But she forgot about that hole in the duster.
He has wriggled out and run away; and he is dancing a jig on the top of the cupboard!

blocks.text: He has wriggled out and run away; and he is dancing a jig on the top of the cupboard!
